title: Markdown Preview Handler displays emoji instead of rendering bold text when using French punctuation

known_information: The reporter supplies a complete Markdown sample, screenshots and diagnostics from PowerToysv0.102.3001.0 on French Windows11. The minimal failing text is **Version :**1.0.

The supplied Markdown handler log reports initialization success; the diagnostic configuration was inspected privately. No crashing handler or missing enablement is established by this rendering symptom.
Product MarkdownHelper explicitly enables UseEmojiAndSmiley with its default enableSmileys=true; the declared dependency is Markdig.Signed0.34.0.

The exact declared parser dependency and product extension configuration were executed against the supplied sample and five controls. With smileys enabled, **Version :** renders as literal opening markers plus an emoji. With enableSmileys=false, it renders as strong text while :smile: still expands.
issue_context.analysis: A parser-level formatting collision is reproduced independently, not inferred solely from a screenshot. The smiley matcher consumes :* from the closing bold delimiter after the French-spaced colon. A focused shortcode-preserving correction is supported; full Explorer/custom image policy/WebView integration and the intended compatibility policy for plain emoticons remain to be verified.
inferences: The same parser collision explains the reported Preview Pane symptom, but full installed-handler integration was not executed in this investigation.

Confirmed named shortcode expansion remains active with smileys disabled; this is not a recommendation to remove all emoji support or globally rewrite colons/asterisks.
